policy_title: Extend Public Interest Test for Company Takeovers
stated: Extend the scope of the existing ‘public interest’ test when considering approvals for takeovers of large or strategically significant companies by overseas-based owners to recognise the benefits to the UK economy, workers and consumers of protecting UK companies from speculative or short-term interests.

source.quote: Extend the scope of the existing ‘public interest’ test when considering approvals for takeovers of large or strategically significant companies by overseas-based owners to recognise the benefits to the UK economy, workers and consumers of protecting UK companies from speculative or short-term interests.

bearing_set.reason: Policy explicitly names workers as a protected group; blocking speculative/short-term overseas takeovers is directly aimed at preventing restructuring, job cuts, or offshoring that damage employment quality and security.

Extending the test to 'strategically significant companies' is a national-security and economic-resilience measure, protecting critical sectors from foreign control that could expose them to external threat or disruption.

Two-sided effect on aggregate prosperity: protecting strategically significant firms from short-termist owners can preserve domestic R&D and long-term investment capacity, but expanded screening also risks chilling beneficial FDI inflows — a genuinely contested, non-negligible tradeoff on productivity and economic opportunity.

membership_note: Two real bearings: O4 (workers, via the stated protection rationale) and O13 (aggregate prosperity, via the FDI/strategic-investment tradeoff). Cost-of-living effects (O2) and national-security effects (O5) are either already covered by existing legislation or too indirect to clear the non-negligible bar. O10 (property rights) is marginal — the restriction on shareholders' right to sell is real but characteristically treated as a regulatory matter rather than a personal-liberty bearing in this policy context.
